![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/18919dad766971de40e8d9e204ac6dc0a811fc3d8857e87e776636f839e83eaa.png)

Use the model above to determine the missing fraction in the following division problem.

$$
1÷\frac{3}{4}=1\,\frac{\boxed{\,\,}}{\boxed{\,\,}}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let's start by interpreting our model:

- The model shows $1$ whole split into quarters.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/a2d50ab7d44607b616d4332abcd114b489462e72843ce90b6405a23364917759.png)

- There are $3$ quarters in each group, with $1$ remaining.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/7bda99628d44b1474fc7416e1a6ceb3e79291e85bbfa337a05b4d778e592c062.png)

Note the following: 

- There is $1$ full group.

- There is $1$ quarter left over out of a possible group of $3.$ So the fractional part of our answer is 

$$
\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
1÷\frac{3}{4}=1\,\frac{1}{3}.
$$
